import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 452

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/452](https://www.erdosproblems.com/452)
-/

namespace Erdos452

open scoped ArithmeticFunction.omega

/-- The greatest length of an interval in $[x,2x]$ on which
$\omega(n) > \log\log n$ everywhere. -/
noncomputable def largeOmegaIntervalLength (x : ℕ) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact Nat.findGreatest
    (fun len ↦ ∃ start, x ≤ start ∧ start + len ≤ 2 * x + 1 ∧
      ∀ n ∈ Finset.Ico start (start + len),
        Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)) < (ω n : ℝ))
    (x + 1)

/-- Determine the largest length of an interval in $[x,2x]$ on which
$\omega(n) > \log\log n$ everywhere. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_452 : largeOmegaIntervalLength = answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

end Erdos452

reformulations.difference: The source asks for the largest qualifying integer interval in [x,2x]. Lean computes a bounded maximum of lengths using half-open runs and the endpoint bound start + len ≤ 2*x + 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For len > 0, put a = start and b = start + len - 1. The Lean conditions are precisely x ≤ a ≤ b ≤ 2*x, with every integer in [a,b] qualifying and cardinality b + 1 - a = len. Conversely, every such closed integer interval gives an admissible run. Length zero is always admissible via an empty run. Every admissible length is at most x + 1, so the findGreatest cutoff excludes nothing and its zero convention is harmless. The scratch file proves this correspondence, the greatest-length characterization, and the resulting equivalence for an arbitrary answer function.
